### CO15 remediation and bounded AD11 Course read — 24 November 2026

The follow-up starts at PR #285 head `ea864b210dbb2caad50a5a46a25399875c0ab3a0`, containing
`main` `670383b92f428e2219f36f615e4dcc79f2febe48`. The Project Leader's explicit instruction
**“CodeMastery — PR #285: Complete CO15, Add AD11 Course Read, Remediate Findings”** authorizes
the implementation, supporting tests, bounded technical choices and minimal runtime extension,
with Course owner @TamiaoNguyen's consent. No higher contract, migration, dependency or REST
operation changes; OpenAPI and frontend types therefore need no change.

**AD11 handoff:** `public LearnerCourseState readLearnerState(UUID courseId)` in the existing
Course `LessonProgressService`. CT03 `requireLearnerCourseAccess` runs before Course business
reads and uses its existing `permitsLearning` (ACTIVE or COMPLETED). CT01 supplies the current
Learner; no caller-supplied learner identifier. Missing/hidden Course is concealed as 404;
LEFT/absent membership on a published Course is 403; Instructor/Administrator is 403. Tests
observe authentication 401 and those mappings through the existing `/progress` admission/REST
boundary, without adding a route for this internal method. A published different Course with
no membership is 403, not 404.

**Transaction choice within the bounded authorization:** MANDATORY plus read-only
REPEATABLE READ metadata checks. A joined transaction ignores the annotation's isolation and
read-only declarations, so the method explicitly rejects incompatible contexts before admission.
MANDATORY requires the caller to own the snapshot; REQUIRED could start an unintended standalone
snapshot, while REQUIRES_NEW would split the composition's snapshot. No root check/marker,
root write lock, write transaction, mutation, event, reconciliation or automatic replay is added.
The method reuses `executionState` and `publishedLessonPlacements`, returning self identifiers,
stored membership/configuration and only published Lessons with actual flags, false/false for
absent progress, canonical Chapter/Lesson order and unchanged positions/gaps.

**Deep immutability:** persistence mapping already deep-copies JSON, but it cannot enforce a
public record's invariant on direct construction or a different provider path. The record now
uses existing `Course.immutableJsonObject`; nested maps/lists and the Lesson list are copied and
unmodifiable, null settings and JSON nulls are preserved, and decimal values retain their approved
representation. A mutable-source regression checks original and returned objects at every level.

**Runtime correction:** [CT17-P6-PRIVILEGES-2026-11-24-r11](deployment.md#ct17-p6-privileges-2026-11-24-r11--co15-atomic-progress-within-the-adr012-192-ceiling-24-november-2026)
adds only UPDATE (mastery_skipped), within ADR012 §19.2. The prior matrix could insert a new skip
but failed with 42501 when the actual adapter upgraded an existing incomplete row. This is
reproduced with the pre-r11 Course privileges and fixed with the exact r11 Course subset.
No claim about privileges currently provisioned on the real VM is made.

| Additional obligation | Actual regression evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Admission first; identity/provider failures propagate without Enrollment/configuration reads; no write or lock call on a learner read | `LessonProgressServiceTest.learnerState*`, with ordered calls and no further interactions |
| ACTIVE/COMPLETED, same-Course published-only placements, ordering gaps, manual/skipped/absent flags and stored adaptive settings | `EnrollmentIntegrationTest.learnerStateReadsPublishedCanonicalPlacementsActualFlagsAndStoredSettingsWithoutWrites` |
| Genuine read-only REPEATABLE READ; no root marker/lock, assigned write xid or state transition; method joins an existing snapshot across a concurrent commit of publication, Enrollment, placement and settings | `learnerStateReadsPublishedCanonicalPlacementsActualFlagsAndStoredSettingsWithoutWrites`, `learnerStateKeepsAccessEnrollmentPlacementsAndConfigurationInTheCallersSingleSnapshot` |
| Restricted-role read-only admission and state read, including CT03's column-limited material lookup | `learnerStateAlsoWorksReadOnlyUnderTheRestrictedRuntimeCoursePrivileges` |
| Actual participant insert, incomplete-row update, manual-label preservation, repeated skips and post-write Enrollment status under the restricted role | `actualParticipantSqlWorksUnderR11AndRollsBackMidBatchFailureWithEnrollmentAndCallerWrites` |
| Injected PostgreSQL failure after an earlier progress update rolls that update and the caller's resume write back; later caller failure rolls inserted progress and status back | the same test, plus `callerFailureRollsBackTheMasterySkipWithTheWholeUnit` |
| No thread/transaction marker leak; wrong isolation/read-only rejected even with a marker; root wait against concurrent manual completion preserves its manual label | `executionParticipationRejectsReadSnapshotsAndDoesNotLeakTheRootToAnotherThreadOrTransaction`, `masterySkipWaitsForManualCompletionOnTheRootAndDoesNotRelabelItsCommittedRow` |
| Pre-r11 UPDATE fails with 42501 and rolls back; r11 still denies identifier/ancestry rewrites, DELETE and TRUNCATE | `actualIncompleteRowUpdateFailsWith42501UnderThePreR11RoleAndNothingCommits`, `r11StillDeniesProgressIdentityRewritesEraseAndTruncate` |
| Only approved Adaptive composition callers; Course never reads mastery or accesses another module's persistence | `participantMethodsHaveOnlyTheApprovedCallers`, `learnerStateHasOnlyTheApprovedAdaptiveReadCallers`; focused source review |

The NOLOGIN roles in the Java tests hold exactly the relevant Course rows, not the bootstrap
superuser's privileges. Write-test roles/ACLs are created inside rolled-back transactions;
the read-only test creates its role outside the read unit and removes its grants/role in `finally`.
The containment suite separately exercises the complete provisioned runtime matrix.

**Remaining upstream work (not absorbed):** no additional missing upstream implementation was
necessary for these two Course deliverables, so no less-than-20% exception was used. The remaining
AS07 profile read is a substantive independent capability (set-based candidate/whole-membership
filter, immutable profile, transaction/caller allowlist and B8-P09 tests); implementing it here
would absorb much of AS07's Final-specific dependency, not just a shared-file helper. AD16's
learner mastery reads and any query-specific runtime SELECT extension must ship with that consumer
and its tests; r8 already permits SELECT (user_id, skill_id, state), but not SELECT (id) or SELECT *.
AD11 still needs its practice selector, `RecommendationService` read composition, controller/DTO
and real endpoint tests. The pure decision engine/resolver and AD14 append service present on this
base do not deliver that endpoint. `readOwnedLearnerState` serves different CT33 consumers and is
excluded. These responsibilities remain with AS07 #158, AD16 #171 and AD11 #168, respectively.

**Not covered and still gated:** Adaptive execution (AD13 #169), Assessment event publication
(AS12 #161), Attempt lifecycle (AS08 #159), the Course assessment guard entries (ADR007 §3.1) and full QA04
`MasteryProgressTransactionIntegrationTest` are still missing on this base. Participant tests
therefore acquire/mark the real Course root directly; they do not prove the missing guard callback
or full quiz-result/mastery/progress/history transaction. LD-11 joint owner review, independent
CODEOWNER review, required CI, protected integration and the ADR011 §5 operational/QA gates
remain separate. Author-side code completeness does not satisfy the whole CO15 Issue DoD or
establish full AD11 integration, release or deployment readiness.

privilege-matrix or frontend change.

**Pure rules.** `AdaptiveDecisionEngine.decide` and `NextLessonResolver` (test-out, remedial-first,
continue), `AdaptiveDecisionEngine.prerequisiteWarnings` (US-06 warning, guidance only) and
`PracticeDifficultySelector` (mapping, fallback order and the §19.4 `recommendPractice` rule with both
fixed English reasons). `PracticeDifficultyProvider` keeps no production caller.

**REST binding (`b8ReadPracticeRecommendation`).**
`GET /api/courses/{courseId}/lessons/{lessonId}/practice-recommendation` in `RecommendationController`
(DTOs in `RecommendationResponse`), composed by `RecommendationService.readPracticeRecommendation` in
one read-only REPEATABLE READ transaction: CT33 `readLearnerState` (CT03 admission, ACTIVE/COMPLETED)
first; then the Lesson must be one of that state's published Lessons (else 404); with the stored
`adaptiveEnabled` false or no Course skill mapped to the Lesson the result is null and nothing else is
read; otherwise Adaptive's `SkillRepository` skills and mappings, the AD16 state read and Assessment's
`readPracticeQuizProfiles` for exactly the Lesson's skills feed `recommendPractice`. The route rule in
`SecurityConfig` requires authentication only, so malformed UUIDs and query parameters are 400 before
the Learner-role 403 that CT03 decides. Success and MVC errors carry `Cache-Control: no-store`.
OpenAPI marks only this operation implemented.

**AD16 read slice.** `LearnerSkillMasteryRepository.findStates` (one native
`SELECT skill_id, state … WHERE user_id = ? AND skill_id IN (…)`, within the r8 column grant, no entity
load) and `MasteryQueryService.readStates` (joins only a read-only REPEATABLE READ caller transaction;
every requested skill returned, an absent row as Unknown). The Mastery Map, guidance, insights and
their REST operations remain AD16's.

## PR #273 audit remediation verification — 25 November 2026

A read-only audit of PR #273 at `be522b4` found these defects. They are fixed on the same pull request under the Project Leader's implementation authorization:

- **N1:** a failed `getOwnedSkillGraph` read on the `Questions` view was retried continuously, about 500 requests per second. The course editor context changed identity on every render, and the stale-refresh path also reloaded after an error. `useOwnedSkillGraph` and `useOwnerRead` now return memoized values. `refreshSkillsIfStale` reloads only after an S20 skill change, and not while a read is in flight. A failed read is retried only by `Try again` or a later deliberate opening.
- **N2:** at 320 to 390 px the Assessments section grew to its segmented switch's min-content width. The canvas clips horizontal overflow, so the assignment cards were cut off. The section and view containers now use `minmax(0, 1fr)` with `minWidth: 0`.
- **N3:** the S20 skill form ran several CT05 writes. A refusal after an earlier commit was reported as a plain failure. Edge additions now run first, because a CT05 409 on `addCoursePrerequisite` means a new cycle. Removals and the name and description follow. The first failure stops the sequence with no compensating write. The message names what was saved, what was refused and how many changes were not attempted. The graph is re-read, and the draft stays on screen. A created skill whose prerequisite is refused stays bound to the form, so saving again edits it instead of creating a duplicate.
- **N4:** the graph canvas showed `0 questions` for every skill, although CT05 returns no question references. Production now passes no count, and the canvas shows and names a count only when its source supplies one. The preview fixtures keep theirs.
- **N5:** primary navigation, the CodeMastery home link and the account menu's `Profile` item left a dirty quiz or assignment editor without asking. A scoped shell navigation guard (`ShellNavigationContext` in `layouts/DashboardLayout.tsx`, provided by `Workspace`) lets the editors and the course editor frame show their existing `Leave without saving?` dialog. The router is unchanged. Browser Back (A15), sign-out and session end are not intercepted.
- **N6:** focus fell to `<body>` after a keyboard map or unmap in `Lesson mapping`. After the re-read, focus returns to the row's `Add skill` control. If that control is disabled, it goes to a chip's remove control, and otherwise to the lesson title.
- **N10:** `sameAssignment` compared deadlines with `Date.parse`, which keeps only milliseconds. `sameInstant` now compares RFC 3339 instants exactly to the microsecond.
- **N9:** the AS09 descriptions in `docs/api/openapi.yaml` and the FE15 record above now state that owner assignment writes lock the Assignment row `FOR UPDATE` in a `READ COMMITTED` transaction without the Course-root guard, as ADR010 §10 requires. Earlier text claimed CO14's Course-root lock. The backend is unchanged.

N7 is unchanged. DESIGN.md S19/S20 ask for the server's detail and field errors. The backend returns only CT18.minimum generic details, with no `errors[]`, and the shared client keeps no server text. This stays a contract mismatch pending a Leader decision. The QuestionEditorSheet test now asserts the production 400 at form level, and labels its field-error case as hypothetical.

## PR #273 U1–U6 remediation verification — 25 November 2026

An ultrareview of PR #273 at `49eaff6` reported findings U1–U8. The Project Leader's instruction "CodeMastery — PR #273: Independent Finding Verification & Autonomous Remediation" (25 November 2026) authorized independent verification and remediation on the same pull request. Each finding was re-verified against source, contracts and runtime evidence:

- **U1 (confirmed, fixed):** the runtime privilege matrix lacked grants that the AS09 owner slice (added here) and CO06 authoring (on `main` since `75cdb8b`, first reachable from the UI here) execute. The real-backend test under the restricted role then found two failures. First, `PUT /api/instructor/courses/{id}` returned 500, because every CO06 owner response reads all nine `learning_materials` columns while the role held three. Second, the AS09 owner count needs `submissions.id`, because Hibernate renders `count(s.id)`. Dated revision `CT17-P6-PRIVILEGES-2026-11-25-r12` ([deployment record](deployment.md#ct17-p6-privileges-2026-11-25-r12--co06-authoring-and-as09-owner-assignments-within-the-adr012-192-ceiling-25-november-2026)) adds exactly the exercised privileges inside the ADR012 §19.2 ceiling, and `deploy.sh` and the three VM tests change with it.
- **U2 (confirmed, fixed):** `useOwnerRead` and `useOwnedSkillGraph` set the body to `null` on any failed re-read, so a background re-read failure replaced the whole course editor with an error view and discarded open drafts. Now only an unknown outcome (network, invalid response, 5xx) of the same key and session keeps the last body, together with the error. 401, 403, 404 and every other refusal, a key change and a session change still discard it. The course editor shell and the assignment editor show "We couldn't load this course. The last loaded version is shown." with `Try again`. The Skills section shows the D12-3 alert "Skills couldn't be loaded." with `Try again`. Nothing is retried automatically. The shared context's skills-stale flag now clears only on a successful read.
- **U3 (confirmed, fixed):** `CreateCoursePage` registers with the shell navigation guard. Back, Cancel, primary navigation, the home link and account-menu links share one `Leave without saving?` dialog. A successful creation clears the draft before it replaces the URL. Sign-out and session end are not intercepted.
- **U4 (confirmed, fixed):** after a deletion empties the current page, the Questions view moves once to the last page the server reports. It acts only on a current, successful read of that page, and each step lowers the page. An empty answer at page 0 shows the empty state.
- **U5 (initially reported fixed; D1 follow-up below):** the initial change keyed the Settings form by course identity and preserved `Saved` on the ordinary post-save re-read. The subsequent independent review at `3f7c184` found that a delayed PUT response could suppress metadata already observed by a shared GET (D1); the original completion claim did not cover that interleaving. An unknown save outcome was not reported as `Saved`.
- **U6 (confirmed, fixed):** a deadline such as `9999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00` normalizes to year 10000 in UTC. `Instant.toString()` then renders `+10000-01-01T04:59:59Z`, which the frontend decoder (four-digit year) and RFC 3339 reject. Create and replace now answer 400 unless the UTC instant lies in years 0000–9999. The check runs in the request parser and again in `AssignmentService`. Microsecond precision and the API format are unchanged. OpenAPI states the rule.
- **U7, U8 (deferred):** the duplicated read and mutation hooks and the duplicated API decoders are maintainability debt, not defects. U2 needed the same small change in both read hooks. Merging them would add a dependency from `skill-graph-editor` to `course-management`, whose hooks already import `skill-graph-editor`, for no correctness gain. No refactor was made.

**Historical persistence claim corrected by D2:** the original boundary test checked symmetric application round-trips for three selected values and their SQL order. It did not prove correct stored UTC instants or universal ordering/round-trip behavior. The subsequent independent review at `3f7c184` found that `0000-01-01T00:00:00Z` stored SQL epoch `-62167046400` instead of `-62167219200`, and `1500-03-10T00:00:00Z` failed with SQLSTATE `22008`. D2 corrects the Assignment-local mapping and replaces that insufficient oracle as recorded below. No conclusion about every other timestamp mapping is established by these Assignment tests.

## PR #273 D2 Assignment UTC persistence follow-up — 25 November 2026

The same explicit D1/D2 implementation authorization covers this Assignment-only correction.
`AssignmentEntity.deadline_at` now selects a nested `DeadlineJdbcType`: the existing Hibernate
JDBC 4.2 OffsetDateTime binder supplies INSERT and targeted JPQL definition UPDATE values, while
an ISO-text extractor constructs the proleptic Gregorian date with PostgreSQL BC converted to
ISO year zero before date validation. This avoids both the previous hybrid-calendar conversion
and the driver's OffsetDateTime-reader failure on the valid `0000-02-29` leap day. The text reader
accepts the driver's ISO timestamps with fractional seconds and offsets including historical
seconds; tests cover UTC, America/New_York and Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh, including local calendar years
outside the UTC representation bounds.

The domain/entity API remains `Instant`, the physical column remains `timestamptz`, and the
normalized UTC years 0000–9999 and microsecond validation are unchanged. AssignmentMapper,
AssignmentService, parser/REST shape, SQL column lists, READ COMMITTED writes, native FOR UPDATE
and REPEATABLE READ owner snapshots are unchanged. There is no global Hibernate setting,
dependency, migration, new repository file, grant or contract amendment.

Verification uses real disposable PostgreSQL. The durable repository tests independently check
SQL `extract(epoch)` using exact BigDecimal arithmetic after INSERT and targeted UPDATE, then
store PostgreSQL text literals and verify extraction through JPQL, native paging and native lock
plus refresh. Fifteen values cover both boundaries, ISO year-zero leap day, historical century
rules, the exact 1500-03-10 failure, dates on both sides of the 1582 cutover and its intervening
ISO dates, microseconds and a modern date. A separate SQL ordering/range-comparison case covers
historical and modern instants. The HTTP test checks create, replace and a fresh GET for six
representative values, along with independent SQL epoch assertions.

**Existing-data compatibility:** no stored data is rewritten. A row previously written by the
incorrect mapping may contain a shifted SQL instant even when the old symmetric reader returned
the intended input. The new reader returns the actual persisted instant, so such a row can now
produce a different historical deadline. Correctly stored PostgreSQL values now read correctly.
An operator must separately audit provenance and intended deadlines before any repair: neither
a blanket date offset nor an automatic migration is authorized. No existing host or production
data was inspected, and this task establishes no count of affected rows.

## PR #273 D1-R1 acknowledgment and reconciliation correction — 25 November 2026

The Project Leader explicitly authorized this focused correction in the same review session:
"PR #273 — Focused D1-R1 Remediation in the Current Independent Review Session". The preceding
independent review at `00f8084` found that the D1 follow-up above was only partially correct.
Its object-identity and metadata-equality branches cannot establish database commit order:

- **GET before the PUT commit:** PUT A is delayed before its guarded write; B commits and a
  publication-triggered shared GET observes B; A then commits and returns successfully. If the
  post-save GET fails, the old form adopts B, becomes clean and says `Saved` although A is stored.
- **Restored original metadata:** A commits, another writer restores the original X, and a shared
  GET observes a new X snapshot before A's delayed reply arrives. If the post-save GET fails,
  equality with the pre-save metadata suppresses X and the old form displays A with `Saved`.

The first sequence is a regression introduced by the earlier D1 fix; the second is a residual.
The original D1 sequence (A commits, B commits, GET B arrives before A's reply) can have exactly
that same frontend response ordering. An immediate choice of A in one case and B in another is
therefore not a valid oracle without additional server ordering metadata. This correction adds
no such metadata or public contract. The earlier implementation and test results above remain
historical records, not proof that D1-R1 was already resolved.

**Reconciliation model.** The existing `useSharedCourseState` counts actual `getOwnedCourse`
initiations. The one existing `useOwnerRead` carries the successful body and that initiation
sequence together; loading, retained-body errors and cancelled/superseded results cannot advance
successful-read evidence. The generic owner-read hook itself is unchanged. Course reload returns
the minimum next initiation sequence and schedules the existing shared reload. Reloads coalesced
by React need no extra GET; a later accepted publication-triggered read can also satisfy the bound.

A successful Settings PUT immediately displays its acknowledged canonical metadata and clears
only the actual draft's dirty state. It starts the existing post-save shared reload and waits for
a current successful read with an initiation sequence at least that bound. Pre-acknowledgment GETs
cannot reconcile this save, irrespective of their values, object identity or arrival time. While
pending the status is `Settings saved. Refreshing course…`; after an unknown read failure it is
`Settings saved, but the current values couldn't be loaded.` The existing stale-course alert and
`Try again` perform one deliberate shared re-read, never a mutation replay. A successful eligible
read reconciles a clean form with the header and restores `Saved`, including when the read returns
the original values or an identical object in a test double. It establishes only the state observed
by that read, not permanent global freshness.

A new unsaved draft retains its fields and the existing dirty-navigation guard. A confirmed save
awaiting reconciliation alone is not an unsaved draft and does not trigger that guard. Consecutive
saves obtain their own causal bounds. Course/session replacement, unmount, cancellation, refusals
and unknown mutation outcomes retain their existing behavior. The form remains keyed by Course
identity. The two qualified status strings are the minimal presentation adjustment authorized for
D1-R1; they do not resolve N7 or amend DESIGN r13, S18/D12-3 or CT21.authoring.

**Executed verification** (isolated implementation clone, starting `00f8084`; cwd `frontend/`):

| Command | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm test -- src/features/instructor/course-management/pages/assessmentAuthoring.test.tsx -t D1-R1` before production changes | 18 new component cases: 16 failed, 2 passed, 55 old cases excluded by selector; exit 1. The two existing-behavior passes are confirmed read refusals. |
| `npm test -- src/features/instructor/course-management/hooks/assessmentHooks.test.tsx src/features/instructor/course-management/pages/assessmentAuthoring.test.tsx src/routes/index.test.tsx` after correction | 3 files, 184 tests passed; exit 0. Includes 18 new component cases and 4 course-context hook cases. |
| `npm run build` | TypeScript and production build passed; exit 0; existing chunk-size advisory. |
| `git diff --check` | Passed; exit 0. |

The deterministic component matrix covers both D1-R1 sequences and original D1 with network,
protocol and 503 reconciliation failures, asserts acknowledgment and qualified status before a
later GET can conceal errors, then verifies explicit retry, successful adoption and no PUT replay.
Further cases cover pre-acknowledgment and post-acknowledgment publication reads, superseded reads,
consecutive saves, reads resolving on either side of a later acknowledgment, same-value snapshots,
clean navigation while unresolved, Course/session replacement and confirmed read refusals.
Existing draft, mutation cancellation, unknown-outcome and navigation tests remain. The original
D1 test now checks the pending acknowledgment before allowing the eligible read to succeed; its
former immediate-ordering claim is intentionally replaced, not accepted as an achievable guarantee.
Hook tests establish success-only evidence, retained errors, same-object success, coalesced reloads,
supersession, Course/session isolation, Strict Mode and unmount cancellation.

**Retained independent evidence and selective omissions.** At `00f8084`, the preceding independent
review passed 42 Assignment unit tests, 29 persistence cases and 3 HTTP cases, plus an independent
14-date SQL-epoch matrix with text/binary prepared-result transfer and a non-UTC JVM. The real
restricted-role backend consumer and V008-to-V009 upgrade harness passed with no 42501. That is
prior independently established evidence, not new-head execution: D2 production/tests, backend,
schema, grants, provisioning and dependencies are unchanged, so none was rerun for D1-R1. The
historical-row compatibility limitation above remains a separate provenance/repair decision.

Standalone containment is retained from the independent `3f7c184` run for unchanged ACL/provisioning,
schema and containment scripts. Full frontend/backend suites, full browser/E2E and interactive
browser checks are omitted: only course-context read evidence and Settings reconciliation changed,
with actual hooks/routes and deterministic interleavings tested above; existing unrelated author
or CI results are not relabeled as new-head independent acceptance. HTTPS, MinIO, containerd,
security scans and release qualification are omitted because their implementations, dependencies
and image baselines are unchanged. No release, deployment or actual-host result is inferred.

These are remediation-author tests and focused self-review. New independent acceptance, Leader

## PR #273 D1-R2 Settings tab lifecycle correction — 25 November 2026

The Project Leader explicitly authorized focused D1-R2 implementation, verification, commit and
push in the existing third independent delta-review session, starting from `77b3128`:
"PR #273 — Focused D1-R2 Remediation in the Current Review Session". This record preserves the
preceding review and remediation records as history. The third independent review verified the
original D1 and D1-R1 causal reconciliation cases and retained independent D2 evidence, but found
D1-R2 (P2, high confidence). D1-R2 also reproduces at `00f8084`: it is a pre-existing lifecycle
issue, not a regression caused by the read sequence counter.

**Reproduction and cause.** The Course provider survives tab changes; the Settings form does not.
With shared metadata X, a successful metadata PUT acknowledges A. While its post-acknowledgment
GET remains pending or fails (503, network or protocol), the old form holds A and its reconciliation
bound only locally. Settings → Content → Settings loses that local state, initializes from retained
X and loses the qualified save status. Editing only description then sends a full replacement with
title X, silently undoing A. The failed branch still has the generic stale-course alert; the pending
branch has no warning after remount. Preserving just a `Saved` label would not correct the payload.

**Correction and ownership.** `useSharedCourseState`, owned by the existing Course provider, retains
only the three acknowledged metadata fields (`title`, `description`, `prerequisiteDescription`) and
the existing minimum read-initiation bound. This state is separate from `course.data` and
`successfulRead`: a PUT never becomes successful GET evidence or a replacement shared Course tree.
The existing GET sequence and reload mechanism are unchanged. The provider resolves the
acknowledgment when an accepted successful read reaches the bound, even while Settings is absent.
An eligible read that returns another writer's values, including the original X, takes precedence;
no object equality or response-order heuristic establishes commit order or permanent freshness.

A remounted Settings form uses unresolved acknowledged metadata as its editing baseline and keeps
`Settings saved. Refreshing course…` or `Settings saved, but the current values couldn't be loaded.`
The existing `Try again` performs one shared read. Tab changes start no additional Course/skill
reads. Later successful saves establish their own bounds. Unsaved drafts, dirty flags, validation,
field errors and unknown-mutation-outcome warnings remain local to the form: an explicitly discarded
draft never reappears as an acknowledgment. A rejected/unknown second mutation does not replace a
previous confirmed acknowledgment with its draft. Acknowledgment alone does not trigger the leave
confirmation. Unknown mutations retain the existing deliberate re-read and are never replayed.

The retained state is scoped to authenticated session generation and Course identity. Identity
replacement or logout discards it. A confirmed read refusal discards the shared body and clears
acknowledgment before same-provider recovery; a later successful recovery cannot resurrect it.
Provider unmount discards the state and existing request cancellation rejects late work. The
existing `useOwnerRead` and `useAuthoringOperation` are unchanged. No new provider, store, client,
repository file, public API, dependency, backend/schema/grant change or navigation guard is added.

**Executed author-side verification** (isolated implementation clone; cwd `frontend/` unless noted):

| Command / environment | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm test -- src/features/instructor/course-management/pages/assessmentAuthoring.test.tsx -t D1-R2 --reporter=verbose` using the final new component tests with defective `77b3128` production files | 9 failed, 5 passed, 73 existing cases excluded; exit 1. The five existing-behavior passes cover eligible read completion outside Settings and logout/authentication replacement. |
| `npm test -- src/features/instructor/course-management/hooks/assessmentHooks.test.tsx src/features/instructor/course-management/pages/assessmentAuthoring.test.tsx src/routes/index.test.tsx` | 3 files, 211 tests passed; exit 0. Includes 14 new component cases and 13 new hook cases. |
| Reused third-review scratch `independentReconciliation.test.tsx` and `independentScheduling.test.tsx` against corrected production files | 14 cases passed; exit 0. Both previously failing remount probes now pass; older-read-before-cleanup and coalescing probes remain intact. These probes are external verification artifacts, not repository additions. |
| `npm run build` | Typecheck and production build passed; exit 0; existing chunk-size advisory. |
| Targeted `playwright-cli`, Chrome `157.0.8103.39`, local Vite app with synthetic intercepted HTTP | Pending and 503 remount branches preserve title A and their qualified status. Actual second PUT contains title A with the description-only edit; two deliberate PUTs, no replay. Strict Mode produces two initial Course GETs (one superseded); each save adds one GET, tab remount adds none. |
| `git diff --check` | Passed; exit 0. |

The durable component cases check all three metadata fields, pending/503/network/protocol remount,
actual second PUT payload, superseded first-save responses, eligible second-save reconciliation,
explicit retry without PUT replay, success while Settings is absent (A, another writer, restored X),
repeated Content/Skills/Assessments/quiz/Assignment routes, draft Stay/Leave/discard, rejected and
unknown later writes, logout and authentication replacement. Provider hook cases check separate
PUT/GET provenance, resolution with no Settings form, pending/failed acknowledgment across
403/404 refusal and failed/successful same-provider recovery, Course/session/logout replacement,
late reads, Strict Mode, unmount and remount. Existing D1/D1-R1 tests retain their causal oracle,
including delayed mutations, consecutive saves, clean navigation, supersession and coalescing.
Mocks establish deterministic frontend behavior; the browser exercises the real app, router,
transport and decoders with synthetic HTTP, not real backend commit ordering or deployment.

**Selective omissions and retained evidence.** D2/backend production and tests, PostgreSQL mapping,
configuration/schema, CT17-P6 r12 grants, infrastructure, contracts and dependency/image baselines
are unchanged from `77b3128` and `00f8084`. No backend/calendar/runtime-role/upgrade suite was rerun.
Retain the prior independent `00f8084` results: 42 Assignment unit, 29 persistence and 3 HTTP cases,
14-date exact SQL-epoch/text/binary/non-UTC probes, and restricted-runtime-role consumer/upgrade
verification. The historical-row compatibility/repair decision remains separate. Standalone
containment retains independent `3f7c184` exact-grants, denial, drift, upgrade and failure-containment
evidence because those implementations are unchanged. These are historical independent results,
not newly executed checks at the remediation commit.

Full frontend/backend, full browser/E2E, HTTPS, MinIO, containerd, security and release qualification
were omitted: the delta affects only Course-owned acknowledgment and Settings lifecycle, directly
covered above; no relevant backend, infrastructure, image or dependency change invalidates their
bounded prior evidence. Unaffected U1–U4/U6 dispositions are retained; U7/U8 remain deferred with
the preceding provenance limitations. No omitted suite is claimed to pass at the new HEAD.

### PR #293 independent-review remediation (IR293-01) — 26 November 2026

The comprehensive independent review of `f97af14` requested changes. Finding
IR293-01 (P2) showed three harness false passes. Each was reproduced on that
baseline against disposable Dockerfile copies, native `linux/arm64`, and each
run reported 18/18 and exit 0:

| Control | Baseline mechanism | Independent observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A: the verifier runs the replaced launcher quietly (`>/dev/null 2>&1 \|\| true`) before the digest check | Execution was inferred only from launcher output in the build log, and the expected digest failure satisfied the case | A sentinel that slept 5 s delayed the verifier's `FAILED` line to 5.058 s, against 0.066 s and 0.113 s for other tree mutations |
| B: the verifier no longer runs Maven; a second `RUN --network=none` inside the marked block prints `Apache Maven 3.9.16` | Output of every offline `maven-bootstrap` RUN counted as verifier output | The version line came from step 5/5, not from the verifier at step 4/5 |
| C: a RUN after the end marker overwrites the verified launcher | Extraction stopped at the end marker | The instruction occurs once in the source Dockerfile and zero times in the test copy |

`test-maven-bootstrap.sh` now:

- copies the Dockerfile through the end of the `maven-bootstrap` stage. Exactly one stage of that name is allowed. Before the begin marker, only `WORKDIR` and `COPY` are allowed. The single RUN must directly follow the begin marker, and the end marker must directly follow that RUN. Nothing may follow it in the stage. Heredocs and malformed, duplicated or misplaced markers are refused.
- inserts, in the test copy only, after the begin marker: the case mutation and a test-only `SHELL` wrapper for the unchanged verifier. The wrapper runs the command with `/bin/sh -c`, as the default shell does, records its exit status and exits 0. BuildKit discards a failed step's filesystem, and a cache mount did not persist between builds here, so this is how the record survives an expected failure.
- exports the record and requires status 0 for accepted cases and exactly 1 for rejected cases. A missing or malformed record fails.
- uses a sentinel launcher that creates a marker file in the committed layer. Any marker fails the run, whatever the launcher printed.
- attributes diagnostics only to the final `maven-bootstrap` step and refuses zero or several such steps.
- refuses 11 Dockerfile regressions with the stated reason: Controls A, B and C, an offline RUN before the block, a masked verifier exit status, the expected diagnostic printed by a failed setup step, a missing begin marker, a duplicate end marker, an end marker inside the RUN, markers outside the target and a second target stage.

`backend/Dockerfile`, the production verifier and the workflow are unchanged. The
existing required step runs the 18 cases and the 11 controls; any failure exits
nonzero.

| --- | --- |
| `MAVEN_TEST_PLATFORM=linux/arm64 bash infrastructure/vm/tests/test-maven-bootstrap.sh` (native) | 18 cases and 11 controls pass, exit 0 |
| `bash infrastructure/vm/tests/test-maven-bootstrap.sh` (amd64 under emulation) | 18 cases and 11 controls pass, exit 0 |
| Corrected harness against the Control A, B and C fixtures | All fail, exit 1, no pass line. A: `Unverified Maven launcher executed before verification`. B: `RUN outside the verifier block`. C: `instruction after the verifier end marker` |
| Control A with the 5 s sentinel under the corrected harness | `FAILED` at 5.061 s and the run is refused. The sentinel's output text appears only in the echoed mutation command |
| Extraction, control transforms and attribution under macOS awk and Ubuntu noble mawk | Identical refusals and byte-identical extracted Dockerfiles |

also raised IR293-R2-01 (P3) on the Retry-After description. Both were
reproduced before the correction.

On `5bf8a62`, macOS arm64, the official Apache 3.9.16 archives were served from
a local file mirror to a disposable `MAVEN_USER_HOME`. The Unix Wrapper started
Maven with both pins blank, both absent, the TAR.GZ pin absent or malformed, a
wrong ZIP declaration followed by the correct one, or the pins supplied only
as environment variables. With blank pins it ran a pre-existing installation
from the unpinned cache namespace. A wrong pin, uppercase hex and a ZIP pin
with only a leading-space spelling already failed. Because the Unix Wrapper
read the pins only when they were present, upstream's unpinned path remained
reachable. The PowerShell body also emitted a launcher for absent or blank
pins, an absent, blank or malformed TAR.GZ pin, a space before `=`, and blank
pins with an installation in that namespace.

`mvnw` and the PowerShell body of `mvnw.cmd` now read both pins from the file
before choosing an installation. Each must appear exactly once as
`name=<64 lowercase hex>`. Archive verification always runs before extraction.
The Backend job runs `test-maven-wrapper-pins.sh` before Java setup. The script
copies the committed scripts into disposable projects whose paths contain a
space. It serves a synthetic distribution (not Apache Maven) and a tampered
copy from a local file mirror. For `mvnw`, a minimal `PATH` uses shims to record every download, extraction
and Maven start. Each rejected case must fail for its pin or digest reason
and leave no installation, staging directory or Maven start. The initial
PowerShell oracle checked the post-cleanup state and launcher output; its
extraction-order observation gap is corrected in the follow-up below. Each `mvnw` run
has `stdin` closed, so no run can consume the case list.

### PR #293 PowerShell extraction-order regression remediation — 26 November 2026

Author verification under the Leader's targeted remediation instruction, based on
`a43c6626f47cbcfae95648c089a882040a7c9579`. The production Wrappers, archive pins,
Dockerfiles, Maven Resolver properties and three VM test renames are unchanged.
IR293-R2-01's corrected Retry-After contract remains unchanged.

**Reproduction.** In a disposable copy only, the PowerShell body extracted the
synthetic ZIP before hashing it, removed that early extraction, then retained the
real checksum rejection and trap cleanup. The original harness returned 0 and
`MAVEN_WRAPPER_PIN_TESTS_PASS mvnw=36 powershell=19`. An independent file outside
the installation recorded the early extraction, including W-H10's wrong-digest
archive. This is a test sensitivity failure, not an observed production compromise.

**Observation.** The harness parses a byte-for-byte `.ps1` copy of `mvnw.cmd`
(PowerShell line breakpoints require that extension), retaining `$script=mvnw.cmd`
and the project's `$scriptDir`, and executes its actual AST through
`Invoke-Command -NoNewScope`. Test-only debugger actions record execution of the
single `DownloadFile` statement, entry into the real `Get-FileHash`, continuation
past the mismatch branch, and actual `Expand-Archive` command entry. The
`verified` event is continuation after the real hash comparison, not hash entry
alone. Neither hashing, comparison, extraction nor exception handling is replaced.
Unsupported verification/download structure or missing/malformed events fails.

Every invocation starts fresh observation state in its case directory, outside
`m2/wrapper/dists`, so installation cleanup cannot erase it. The observer emits
no launcher stdout and records only fixed event names. A command breakpoint can
report both entry and process callbacks for `Expand-Archive`: one or more adjacent
`extract` events are permitted after `verified`; callback count is not an exact
count of archive invocations. `download` observes execution of the selected
method-call statement, not a separate network/transport trace. These synthetic
cases use a local file mirror; the Backend workflow does not impose OS network
isolation. The local Linux qualification below additionally uses `--network none`.

| Control | Required events and outcome |
| --- | --- |
| W01 cold ZIP, W03 CRLF, paths containing spaces | `ready download hash verified extract...`; real extraction and fixture publication, exact launcher stdout |
| W02 warm, mirror withdrawn | `ready` only; same trusted installation and launcher |
| Invalid pins, including warm/legacy caches | `ready` only, pin error, no launcher and unchanged cache paths |
| W-H10 wrong digest | `ready download hash` only; checksum error, zero extraction callbacks, no launcher or residual staging/install |
| W-S early extraction, with and without explicit early cleanup | `ready download extract... hash`; both preserve checksum error and complete cleanup, and the same digest oracle must reject their event order |
| W-S missing, malformed, missing-ready and missing-verified evidence | The actual cold-install acceptance oracle must reject each independently altered observation |
| W04 correctly pinned non-ZIP | `ready download hash verified extract...`, real cmdlet failure, nonzero status, no launcher or residual staging/install |

All existing substantive controls remain. There are now 36 Unix cases per shell
when both digest tools are available and 27 PowerShell controls (19 original,
one 64-character inner-space case, four evidence sensitivity controls, two
extraction-order mutations and one failed-extraction control). The existing
mandatory Backend step runs them before setup-java and Maven verification;
missing PowerShell remains fatal there. H06e now substitutes one character with
an internal space, keeping exactly 64 characters. Every Bash condition in this
harness uses `[[ ... ]]` with quoted literal comparisons. Generated POSIX `sh`
launchers and production `backend/mvnw` retain POSIX syntax. The three `eval`
inputs remain checked-in static fixture tables, with generated hexadecimal pins;
no externally supplied command text enters them, and neither Sonar rule flags
these expressions. No framework redesign or suppression was added.

**Executed local evidence:** macOS arm64 Bash 3.2 ran 36 cases each under `sh`,
`dash` and `bash` (108). Linux PowerShell 7.4.6 amd64 under emulation passed

  grid badge whose intrinsic width reserves horizontal space. A 20px-high badge
  sits above the 20px glyph within the header; the circle remains 44px. Below 600px
  that wider utility selects the existing mark-only lockup and 4px slot gaps.
  This is a bounded responsive presentation choice, not a count cap or a global
  breakpoint/token change. Small badges remain inside their circle's horizontal
  bounds. The wide badge is noninteractive; pointer transparency supplements the
  reserved layout, not a substitute for preventing visual overlap. All digits,
  semantic colours, top-bar height and utility order are preserved. Clipping,
  `99+`, numeric truncation, changing DTOs and expanding the interactive circle into
  a wide pill were rejected. There are no other production HeaderIconButton callers
  beyond NotificationBell; existing shared tests cover the unbadged Help consumer.
- **Focus:** on a focused button's keyboard click (`detail === 0`), synchronously
  move focus, with `preventScroll`, to the local named `notification-updates`
  region. Its list/loading/error/empty and pagination children may change without
  removing that owner. The existing `notification-results` list/filter target stays
  separate. Tab continues into available row/retry/pagination controls; Shift+Tab
  returns to the selected filter. Pointer clicks retain native focus behaviour.
  No delayed focus callback can reclaim focus after user movement, route departure,
  unmount, logout, session/account replacement or eligibility loss. No old list data,
  async operation ticket, provider, hook, transport or mutation policy is added.
  Retaining stale rows, modifying shared PaginationBar and restoring focus after an
  async response were unnecessary alternatives. Existing success/empty/unknown-count
  copy and S01–S03 remain unchanged.

### Second-round IR296-D01/D02 author qualification — 26 November 2026

**Review history.** The full-scope review of `031dbff` issued REQUEST_CHANGES
for IR296-01/02/03. The first author remediation ended at
`10bcc9c6b751c54c8e0e36ccfa16072bc237d30c` (six PR commits, 37 files,
+3553/-101; main/merge-base `cc6cb54ddedf226966a51c9614fc5fc5756267bb`).
The subsequent independent narrow-delta review independently VERIFIED_FIXED
IR296-01 and IR296-02, but assessed IR296-03 as PARTIALLY_FIXED and confirmed
P2 findings IR296-D01 (late physical commit) and IR296-D02 (suppressed cleanup
failure). The preceding first-round author claims are historical, not independent
closure. This second round changes only this integration test and testing records.

**D01 mechanism and correction.** With Spring 7.0.9's actual
`JpaTransactionManager` and Hibernate 7.4.5.Final, returning from a
`TransactionTemplate` callback precedes Spring beforeCommit/beforeCompletion,
JPA commit, Hibernate completion/flush and physical JDBC commit. Checking a flag
in the action callback cannot cancel that later commit. Each worker now owns a
test-local `JpaTransactionManager` using the application's existing
EntityManagerFactory, DataSource, JpaDialect and execution listeners. Its doCommit
runs after Spring synchronizations, explicitly flushes outside the coordination
lock, and then arbitrates admission under the same short lock as cleanup.

The assignment to ADMITTED is the commit-admission linearization point. Cleanup
sets stopping and marks PENDING units CANCELLED under that lock. If cancellation
wins, the callback or doCommit throws `WorkerCancelled`; Spring executes physical
rollback. No action result is returned as a successful cancelled transaction.
If admission wins, cleanup cannot revoke it: JPA/Hibernate/JDBC completion runs
outside the lock and may commit or fail. ADMITTED is permission to attempt commit,
not proof of a successful or irreversible commit. Actual afterCompletion status
is recorded separately. Missing/UNKNOWN completion, failed commit/rollback/resource
cleanup, or a CANCELLED unit that did not roll back makes cleanup qualification
fail, even when Future.cancel has hidden the worker exception. Failures after the
callback, including afterCommit, are retained. An action exception replaced by a
rollback exception remains attached for diagnostics.

The deterministic advisory-lock regression runs actual AttemptService.start,
checks one pending Attempt and two pending Answers inside its transaction, and
blocks real JDBC after the old callback check. The test observes that worker's
PostgreSQL lock wait before starting cleanup. It observes cancellation winning
before releasing the controlled blocker. beforeCommit and beforeCompletion cases
both end CANCELLED/ROLLED_BACK with zero committed Attempts/Answers. The admitted
case ends ADMITTED/COMMITTED with one Attempt/two Answers despite a cancelled
Future. Two additional faults prove that an admitted commit failure rolls back
and fails qualification, while an afterCommit failure reports committed data and
also fails qualification. Neither is misclassified as successful cancellation.

**D02 correction and faults.** Expected-primary qualification checks the exact
expected failure family and rejects suppressed exceptions on the original/cause
chain, preserving the original throwable and its cleanup diagnostics. Four
permanent real-cleanup fault cases delegate physical blocker rollback and then
throw SQLException (SQLState IR296); assertion, timeout, SQL setup and interruption
must each be rejected as failed qualification. A fifth case injects both rollback
and close reporting failures after the real operations; both errors survive
try-with-resources suppression. Cleanup always attempts blocker rollback, blocker
close, task cancellation, executor shutdown and bounded termination, accumulating
secondary errors rather than replacing the first. Resource release, rolled-back
Enrollment mutation, zero partial data and subsequent root reacquisition are
asserted on these fault paths too.

**Executed verification** (backend directory, Temurin 25.0.4.1, disposable hardened
PostgreSQL 17.11 Testcontainers, unchanged V001-V009):

```bash
./mvnw -B -q test-compile failsafe:integration-test failsafe:verify \
  -Dit.test=AssessmentPersistenceIntegrationTest
```

| First corrected source with permanent regressions | 60 | 0/0/0 | All 52 retained cases plus eight new cases pass. |

`git diff --check` passes. All original behavioral assertions remain: concurrent
start/retake, manual/save/expiry, diagnostic winners, definition re-read, the
one-second statement deadline and execution-scope wrong-thread refusal. Blocker
release remains before cancellation/termination waiting. Existing 8-second

The admission lock is never held during JDBC, flush or commit. No sleeps are used.

## FE14 targeted IR-01/IR-02/IR-03 remediation — 26 November 2026

### Baseline, provenance and scope

This append preserves the original implementation verdict and A1–A4 audit above.
The subsequent independent verdict was **REQUEST_CHANGES** at
`e4d7eb3febfad8f89db1b9091c7931ed3308654a` (main/merge-base
`cc6cb54ddedf226966a51c9614fc5fc5756267bb`, 21 files, +1943/-61, two commits).
Remote PR state, both SHAs and legitimate existing heizseung author/committer
metadata were reverified. Remediation uses an isolated shared-object clone; the
clean main checkout, other occupied worktrees and PRs #280/#286 were preserved.
Only additive commits and a normal fast-forward push are authorized.

The previous review's `fe14-review-evidence.zip` was retrieved and inspected,
including `evidence.json` and the four probes. Its executed evidence remains
historical independent evidence. The executions below are **new author evidence**
from Codex-assisted remediation; none is independent acceptance.

### Findings, implementation and focused self-audit

| Finding | Confirmed cause and correction | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FE14-IR-01, P1 | Child unmount aborted sent work before the owner registered recovery. Register the operation/controller synchronously in the existing Course owner; preserve settlement across child routes, suppress child callbacks, sequence authoritative Course/graph recovery and enforce the shared runner entry barrier | FIXED_AUTHOR_VERIFIED |
| FE14-IR-02, P2 | Inspection decoded and stripped the destination that was emitted. Separate inspected spellings from the emitted mdast URL; compare reference kind, standard-parser scheme/origin, validate encoding and retain encoded navigation data and external attributes | FIXED_AUTHOR_VERIFIED |
| FE14-IR-03, P2 | Definition collection inspected only root children. Walk the complete AST in document order, retain first definitions and the parser's normalized identifiers; links/images use the same admission function | FIXED_AUTHOR_VERIFIED |

Owner transitions are `idle -> pending -> recovery-required -> idle` on a
causally eligible successful read. Unknown/cancelled settlement adds a persistent
uncertainty notice; inspection permits a deliberate next attempt under CT16/CT37,
not proof that an unobserved transaction ended. A failed read retains the obligation.
No mutation replay, backend transaction-status contract, timeout, history blocking,
new global state or provider is introduced. Owner/session replacement aborts old
work and rejects its result. Whole-owner navigation keeps the existing CT16 scope;
the fix guarantees survival across child-route changes while that owner remains.

The actual entry-point test invokes all eight Course operations and both S20
mapping operations directly during pending and recovery; every call is refused

  calls, unqualified invocations and method references, and could allow a matching
  basename in another package. Replace it with JDK AST traversal of calls,

  exercise direct/spaced/unqualified/reference syntax and ignore comments,
  strings and longer method names. This was a coverage defect; no unauthorized
  production caller was found.

### D. Incoming findings

All references in this subsection are to incoming `3ab9ee28`; severity is P2.

**IN06-IR-01 — report intake admits malformed hidden ancestry.**
`ContentReportService.java:89–91` checks only whether the immediate parent is visible
and in the Lesson; it does not require a root question. V006 permits deeper chains
and multi-row cycles. A synthetic post below `REPLY_UNDER_HIDDEN` receives 201 and
a persisted report even though Q&A's query correctly excludes it. This violates
CT30's visible-target/depth boundary (§§6.1–6.3), discloses existence and admits an
invisible report target. The adjacent check in `DiscussionService.java:90–93` also
returns a body-field 400 for malformed deeper ancestry instead of concealment.
The normal supported reply-to-reply case remains a 400.

**IN06-IR-02 — escaped lone surrogates silently lose verbatim content.**
`DiscussionService.java:96–100` and `ContentReportService.java:199–204` only check
non-whitespace text. Strict UTF-8 wire decoding in `InteractionRequests.java:19–28`
does not reject JSON-escaped unpaired UTF-16 surrogates. A real POST with
`{"content":"x\ud800"}` returns 201; an independent committed JDBC read finds
second code unit 63 (`?`), versus incoming 55296. The PostgreSQL driver replaced
unencodable text, violating CT30 verbatim storage. The same unchecked String path
applies to report reasons. This is actual data corruption, not a stylistic Unicode
policy. NUL also cannot be stored by PostgreSQL and is covered by the corrected
field validation; valid surrogate pairs and combining text must remain verbatim.

**IN06-IR-03 — whole-body allocation precedes syntax and parser constraints.**
`InteractionRequests.java:19–26` reads all bytes, decodes another whole-body buffer
and only then invokes Jackson. A synthetic stream invalid at its first byte, with
1 MiB of remaining padding, is consumed completely (1,048,577 read attempts) before
400. The supported direct backend binding has no configured JSON body cap; multipart
upload limits do not bound this servlet JSON read. Jackson constraints therefore
cannot protect the preceding allocations. An admitted actor can impose avoidable
memory/resource pressure. No production OOM was induced, and this is not a claim
that every deployed ingress accepts arbitrarily large bodies. The finding rests
on reproduced eager consumption plus the actual supported direct-backend path,
not merely the presence of `readAllBytes()`.

Rejected hypotheses: no lost main SecurityConfig protections remain; CT40's
unlocked multi-statement Course/Lesson publication snapshots are permitted by
ADR012 §§3.1/4.1 and do not require a root lock; IN21 REST/audit is not missing
IN06-owned code; timestamp/clock or genuine database-integrity failures retain
§12's safe 500/rollback behavior. No unrelated Auth defect is remediated here.

### E. Direct remediation

- IR-01: require the immediate ancestor to be a visible same-Lesson **root** in
  report visibility and supplied-reply ancestry. This bounds inspection at depth
  one and conceals deeper/cyclic persisted state without traversing arbitrary
  chains or changing valid reply-to-reply errors. PostgreSQL regressions cover
  hidden ancestry, a synthetic cycle, 404-before-body precedence and zero reports.
- IR-02: `InteractionRequests.isRepresentableText` rejects NUL and unpaired UTF-16
  surrogates; both services apply it at the existing content/reason field stage,
  after actor/Lesson/parent admission. Regressions assert safe field 400/no-store,
  no post/report/notification writes, unchanged 403/404 precedence and actual
  committed verbatim supplementary/combining text. The two OpenAPI request-field
  descriptions explain the representation rule; property sets/types are unchanged.
- IR-03: strict UTF-8 `InputStreamReader` feeds Jackson directly, preserving
  duplicate/trailing-token rejection and existing parser constraints while removing
  whole-wire-body buffering. A synthetic stream asserts early syntax rejection;
  another case accepts 1.1 million text characters and rejects malformed UTF-8
  after a buffer boundary. No arbitrary product text-length limit was added.

Supporting verification changes replace three scheduling-timeout assumptions with
PID publication and `pg_blocking_pids()` observation, retain both parent-lock race
orders, force two distinct-report hides to contend, and add dismissal-first
terminal revalidation and CT40 caller-snapshot coverage. These passed as incoming
production probes before being retained. No stronger production serialization,
new transaction propagation or Course-root lock is introduced.

### F. Transaction, concurrency and security assessment

The real PostgreSQL tests establish that reply and derived-ID notification rows
are invisible to an independent connection before commit, roll back together, and
a notification insert trigger failure rolls back the reply. Recipient, exact
message, self-reply exclusion and publication skips use the existing IN07 service.
The committed-read evidence is not a mock-only atomicity claim.

Parent SHARE versus moderation UPDATE is observed in both race orders. Competing
hides wait on content first; report rows lock by PostgreSQL UUID order. Both
dismissal/hide orders and preloaded stale report revalidation are exercised, with
terminal 409 and rollback instead of reopening. Mutations join the caller's
transaction and reject absent/read-only/explicit non-READ-COMMITTED callers.
IN21 must still hide Lessons under the Course root and append the required audit
rows in its transaction; the Interaction handoff does not claim those end-to-end
Admin guarantees.

CT40 returns only requested/scoped titles and V002 publication literals, handles
missing resources and the 100-ID cap, has no public Course REST binding and uses
the approved caller set. A real REPEATABLE READ caller probe proves participation
in its snapshot. Outside an active transaction its methods run read-only READ
COMMITTED; the contract permits distinct unlocked statement snapshots and a hide
after admission. It does not promise publication remains unchanged until commit.

CT17-P6 r17 changes only SELECT/INSERT and UPDATE(is_hidden) on discussion_posts,
and SELECT/INSERT and UPDATE(status,resolved_at) on content_reports. Restricted
JPA execution, row locks, immutable-column/DELETE/TRUNCATE rejection, cumulative
27-relation matrix equivalence, upgrades and idempotency are tested. No applied
migration, shared/staging/production grant or operational provisioning was changed.

The PID is published through JdbcTemplate inside the same TransactionTemplate and
transaction manager as the production proxy call. JpaTransactionManager-bound JDBC
and JPA therefore use the intended transactional connection. The winner's barrier
keeps its row locks open until pg_blocking_pids observes a database-blocked waiter;
both reply/hide orders, competing hides and dismissal-first terminal revalidation
complete with the required committed result/409. Polling is bounded and is evidence
of a real lock wait, not a fixed scheduling delay. The helper does not name the
blocker or lock relation; isolated fixtures, held winner locks and inspected lock
paths exclude an evidenced competing unrelated wait in these executions. This is
sufficient regression evidence, not a general-purpose lock-graph assertion.

Wrappers join READ COMMITTED production transactions and preserve MANDATORY
moderation participation; no service method is replaced or mocked. Barrier release
and executor interruption run in finally blocks; normal completion joins futures
before fixture cleanup. The synthetic cycle is removed by restoration and the
fixture's set-wise descendant deletion. No timeout or cleanup failure occurred.
The CT40 REPEATABLE READ test observes published context across an independent hide
and hidden context after caller completion, supporting caller-transaction/snapshot
participation. No broader CT32/CT40 review was reopened.

Reader delivery eliminates eager whole-wire buffering and applies existing parser

FE11-IR-02” task, including implementation, regression tests, author self-audit,
documentation, commit and ordinary fast-forward publication to PR #305. Refs #196;

### Baseline and independent history

Incoming/reviewed HEAD: `75b6db7f6c2ed21182806c2f859264e581088908`; live main and
merge-base: `99abc4072b9893971d7cf15fe3174b25b3da63b9`, six ahead/zero behind.

integration was necessary. Both findings remained reproducible. The independent
**REQUEST_CHANGES** verdict on that revision remains historical evidence; the
27 November author code-complete claim above was superseded by that review.
Author remediation does not independently close it.

The complete prior independent report was recovered from its Codex chat. The
reviewer's `fe11-review-evidence.zip` and `review-integrity.json` were accessible;
original `probes/lifecycle-required.test.tsx`, observational sources and logs were
inspected. The unmodified desired-invariant source (only import paths adapted to
the isolated clone) reproduced **7 failures / 2 passing controls** before changes,
and passed **9/9** afterwards. These are recovered probes, not reconstructed cases.
The observational suite asserts obsolete admission as its expected result; it was
inspected, not misreported as a post-fix success suite.

### Corrections and author dispositions

- **FE11-IR-01 — FIXED_AUTHOR_VERIFIED.** The old render-written `snapshot` could
  remain eligible after GET settlement released the read reservation. Every hook
  transition now synchronously publishes one authoritative State object before
  calling `setState`. Read initiation installs loading/checking; accepted success
  installs current data; failure clears data and installs error before release.
  Controller/sequence/resource/session checks still reject obsolete settlements.
  Rendering never writes authority. A layout-effect acknowledgement records only
  a matching committed publication; invocation additionally requires the callback's
  State object to match that publication. Thus even fast PUT/GET settlement cannot
  admit an action before the reloaded file and uncertainty notice are presented.
- The production file-change handler uses the same invocation guard. Replacement
  selection captures filename and the exact opaque submitted-time string; dialog
  copy uses that captured evidence. Current eligibility and matching evidence gate
  the dialog, and refresh/closure/grading/error withdraws it. Old confirmation
  callbacks fail at the hook; repeated confirmation cannot obtain another mutation
  reservation. No `Date` conversion is applied to the token.
- **FE11-IR-02 — FIXED_AUTHOR_VERIFIED.** Remove feature 400/415 explanations and
  consume the shared safe `ApiError.message`: 400 without admitted fields is
  `Please check the supplied information.`; 415 is
  `The request could not be completed.`. Preserve exact 413 copy and 409 wording
  derived from reloaded graded/open state, including neutral eligible-state
  conflict recovery. No shared transport/error allowlist was changed.
- **Adjacent author finding SA-R1 — FIXED_AUTHOR_VERIFIED.** A captured Cancel
  callback read the current mutation ref and could abort a later upload, including
  after resource replacement in a reused hook. Two deterministic tests reproduced
  it before correction. Cancel now checks current identity and the exact controller
  captured for its rendered operation. This is bounded to the same hook.

### Deterministic regression and transition matrix

All committed cases live in the existing `assignment.test.tsx`. Deferred promises,
React `act` scopes and the existing deadline scheduler preserve settlement before
commit; no arbitrary delay, early forced render or weakened dispatch assertion is
used. The production deadline cases drain the original probe's eight promise
microtasks while the old file input/confirmation button is still displayed.

| Ordering / protected invariant | Incoming execution | Remediated execution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reviewer refresh success closed / failure / newly existing submission, old callback before commit | 3 failures: actual PUT dispatched | 3 pass: zero PUT; deliberate successful read recovers legitimate submission |
| Reviewer first PUT + reconciliation complete, old null-token callback before commit | Failure: second unconfirmed PUT | Pass: exactly one PUT; new confirmed replacement still works |
| Reviewer production deadline GET then file-change before closed/replacement/failure commits | 3 failures: actual PUT dispatched | 3 pass: zero PUT and no replacement dialog from obsolete selection |
| Reviewer controls: committed closure; pending server work after cancelled response | Both pass | Both pass; cancellation still does not promise rollback or cause replay |
| Stale hook confirmation after closed/graded/error/changed/same read evidence | 5 failures | 5 pass; new callback required even if token unchanged; adjacent microseconds remain distinct |
| Uncertain network/unusable-success/cancelled settlement then GET before presentation | 3 failures | 3 pass: no second PUT until committed evidence and deliberate action |
| Obsolete production confirmation event after closed/graded/changed/error/same read | 5 failures | 5 pass: zero PUT; no silent filename substitution |
| Shared safe 400/415 fallback | 2 failures | 2 pass |
| Obsolete Cancel against newer same-resource/different-resource upload | 2 failures | 2 pass; newer signal remains un-aborted |
| Active/superseded read cleanup; older read failure versus newer ready data; StrictMode read cleanup; old-route mutation cleanup; logout/unmount; exact 413; neutral 409; duplicate production confirmation | Pass | Pass |

| Corrupt projection fails closed; inputs validated and copied | PARTIAL → PR | COMPLETE | PR range/scale checks, `Objects.requireNonNull` before `Set.copyOf` (mirrors `readOwnedLatestSkillEvidence`) | PR unit tests; snapshot guard now proven to precede input validation |

**Findings and remediation (all test-side; no production defect found).**
AS17-F01 (P2) no oracle separated HALF_UP from HALF_EVEN/truncation (66.67, 50.00,
25.00 and 0.00 are equal under each) — fixed by the 16.665 case. AS17-F02 (P3) the
`started_at` tuple key was unexercised with differing scores — fixed. AS17-F03 (P2) a
later unsubmitted attempt displacing the latest submitted one was untested — fixed.
AS17-F04 (P2) cross-Course exclusion was untested for this read — fixed. AS17-F05 (P3)
100.00 upper bound — fixed. AS17-F06 (P2) read-write and non-RR outer transactions
were rejected only in a unit test with hand-set synchronization flags — fixed with
real proxies. AS17-F07 (P2) snapshot stability under a concurrent commit — fixed.
AS17-F08 (P2) the read had not run under the restricted runtime role — fixed. AS17-F09
(P3) the unit test named “before validation” passed only valid inputs — fixed.
AS17-F10 (P3, documentation) the PR body called the PR's integration fixture
“tie-breaking” although its timestamps differ; tie-break evidence is inherited — PR
body corrected. Observation (not remediated): the population binds one parameter per
learner, so a single Course above the PostgreSQL bind limit (about 65,000 joined
learners) would fail closed rather than return a wrong figure; this is far beyond
project scale and CT13 sets no bound.

step 6 and §12 execution scope (B6-V09), `AS08-ANCESTRY-2026-11-26-r1` (ADR007 §16)

**Implemented boundaries** (existing `QuestionBankService`, no REST, no migration):

| Boundary | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `CoverageSnapshot(UUID courseId, Map<UUID, Long> questionCounts)` | Nested, deeply immutable, no null key/value, nonnegative counts, no answer keys |
| `readCoverage(courseId, skillIds)` | Null Course → `IllegalArgumentException`; only an owner REPEATABLE READ snapshot (its own or joined) or the Course-root READ COMMITTED write unit is accepted, else safe 500 before any query; then CT03 ownership, null set/element rejection, empty → empty map, CT40 `readSkillIds` scope with the same safe 404 for foreign/unknown skills, exact requested keys with explicit zeros |
| `readCoverageForExecution(courseId, skillIds)` | `AttemptService.requireExecutionScope` first (actual read-write READ COMMITTED transaction, Assessment-private marker for this Course on this thread and physical transaction); no actor; empty → empty map without queries; ancestry through the §17 caller, a foreign skill is safe 500 |
| Population (both) | Every stored Question of each requested skill, all kinds and difficulties, used or unused, hidden or published membership, counted once by ID; a row failing V004/data-model §11, a null provider result, a row of an unrequested skill or a repeated ID is an integrity failure, never a zero |
| `QuestionRepository.findAllInSkills` | Assessment-private JPQL over its own `questions` table; materializes rows because a count-only query cannot detect malformed definitions |

## AS18 targeted test remediation (AS18-IR-01, AS18-IR-02) and author self-audit — 28 November 2026

Scope: AS18 #164 in PR #307, under the Project Leader's “Targeted Test Remediation —
AS18-IR-01 & AS18-IR-02” instruction. Test-only: one file,
`AssessmentPersistenceIntegrationTest.java`. This is an author self-audit with AI
assistance (Claude Code), not an independent review. The independent review of
`c03bf2d` (`6fce59d` after the metadata normalization below) returned
`REQUEST_CHANGES` for the two P2 findings. Its other dispositions are unchanged and
remain the reviewer's: AS18-R01 to R05 `VERIFIED_FIXED`, and R06 `PARTIALLY_FIXED`
because of these two findings.

| Finding | Root cause | Remediation |
|---|---|---|
| AS18-IR-01 (P2) | The `CoverageFixture` constructor ran each insert in its own autocommit statement under `NOT_SUPPORTED`. When a statement failed, the earlier rows stayed committed, and try-with-resources never called `close()` on the unconstructed object. The reviewer reproduced this with a `23514` failure on `Hidden only`: an extra Skill and the foreign Course remained, and teardown then failed on `fk_skills_course_id`. | `fixtureTransaction` runs setup in one bounded physical transaction: `READ COMMITTED`, 10 s timeout, `SET LOCAL lock_timeout`/`statement_timeout`. It asserts that it owns that transaction and commits before any worker starts. Cleanup deletes every row the fixture owns, FK-safely, in one bounded transaction, including Questions that workers authored in the fixture's skills. The first AS18 case's extra rows use the same transaction. |
| AS18-IR-02 (P2) | `as18GuardedReadiness…` closed the fixture before shutting down the executor. A worker that timed out while holding a Course root therefore left `DELETE courses` waiting without a bound, and a later Question insert hit `fk_questions_skill_id`. | The authors now run through the existing `AttemptWorkers`, unchanged, which provides physical transaction ownership, PID tracking, `PENDING`/`CANCELLED`/`ADMITTED` commit admission and bounded termination. `CoverageWorkerRun.close()` calls `AttemptWorkers.close()` first: stop admission, release the blocker, cancel, then wait at most 10 s. Fixture rows are deleted only after the executor has terminated, every started worker transaction has completed, and no tracked backend has an open transaction, a lock wait or a lock. The decision depends on this gate, not on whether close succeeded or a Future was cancelled. If quiescence cannot be established, a bounded recovery terminates only this run's tracked worker backends that still hold a transaction or lock wait, then waits up to 5 s. The recovery is always reported as a failure, and fixture cleanup is withheld if the workers are still not quiescent. |

The shared AS08 `assertWorkerResourcesReleased` helper now excludes its own backend
(`pid<>pg_backend_pid()`). The connection pool can hand the probe a worker's
returned connection, and the probe then reported its own statement as a leaked
transaction. This was observed once during this work. A worker connection that is
still in use cannot be handed out, so the exclusion does not weaken the check.

**Regression oracles (real PostgreSQL).**
`as18FailedCoverageFixtureSetupRollsBackEveryFixtureRowAndKeepsTheCourseUsable`
injects a real `ck_questions_kind` (`23514`) failure inside the setup transaction
after each of six milestones: extra Skill, foreign Course, foreign Skill, first
Question, hidden Quiz and first membership. Each case first observes that the
fixture's rows are visible inside the transaction. It then checks, through
independent reads, that none survives, that the AS08 Course is intact (exactly one
owned Course, its Skill, q1/q2 and its Quiz), that a new fixture, an owner coverage
read and a guarded authoring call succeed, and that the outer teardown passes.
`as18WorkerFailurePathsAreBoundedAndCleanFixturesOnlyAfterWorkerQuiescence` covers:

- D1: a timeout while a worker holds the foreign Course root (`FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` → `55P03`) and an uncommitted Question.
- D2: a worker action failure after a write.
- D3: a main-thread failure while a same-Course worker waits for the root.
- D4: interruption, with the flag preserved.
- D6: a blocker rollback fault that the expected primary cannot conceal (`IR296` under `AS18 coverage cleanup failed`).

Each D case requires a bound under 20 s, `CANCELLED`/`STATUS_ROLLED_BACK`, no FK
failure in the worker, rolled-back completions recorded at the gate, no worker
Question, no fixture row, released resources (`assertWorkerResourcesReleased`) and
a later usable Course.

`as18FixtureCleanupWaitsForAnAdmittedWorkerCommitBeforeDeletingFixtureRows` (D5) has
a worker admitted before cancellation and holds its real commit on an advisory
lock. While that commit is held, the cancelled Future, the alive closer, the intact
foreign Course and the absent row prove that cleanup has not started. After
release, the commit completes (`STATUS_COMMITTED` at the gate) before the committed
Question is deleted with its fixture Skill.

`as18NonCooperativeWorkerIsTerminatedBeforeFixtureCleanupAndCannotPass` has a worker
that removes its own timeouts. The test shows that recovery terminates only its
tracked PID, that the primary carries `AS08 workers exceeded the cleanup deadline`
plus the recovery failure, and that cleanup runs only afterwards. The success-path
oracle is unchanged: the same-Course `create` waits on the holder (observed from an
independent connection), the other Course commits meanwhile, the snapshot is stable
while the root is held, and coverage is fresh afterwards. Both workers end
`ADMITTED`/`STATUS_COMMITTED`.

**Executed commands (macOS, Docker 29.8.1, Testcontainers PostgreSQL, JDK 25;
`-Djacoco.skip=true` for focused runs).** Tested revision: `26389e7`, tree
`862225a`. Its metadata-normalized successor `5e22a57` has the identical tree,
so the results apply to it unchanged.

```bash
cd backend
./mvnw -B verify -Dtest=none -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false -Djacoco.skip=true \
  '-Dit.test=AssessmentPersistenceIntegrationTest$TimedAttemptRuntime#as18*+failureBeforeBlockerCommit*+cleanupFailureCannotQualify*+rollbackAndCloseFailures*+jdbcCompletionWait*'
# -> 32/0/0/0: 18 as18* (5 existing + 13 new) and 14 AS08 AttemptWorkers qualification cases
./mvnw -B verify -Dtest=none -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false -Djacoco.skip=true \
  '-Dit.test=AssessmentPersistenceIntegrationTest*'
# -> 97/0/0/0 (84 previous + 13 new), BUILD SUCCESS
# as18* repeated twice more -> 18/0/0/0 each; runaway case about 10.2 s by design, others under 0.4 s
# Mutants (temporary, restored byte-identically):
#   M1 setup without the transaction -> all 6 setup-failure cases fail (1 to 9 leaked rows)
#   M2 fixture cleanup before worker quiescence (pre-remediation order) -> D1 fails
#      (5 s lock timeout surfaces as a concealed cleanup failure) and D5 fails
#      (cleanup never reaches the worker gate); both runs stayed bounded
```
